units.account: Col. Aubry had no new orders. He held his line south of the bridge and rested his men after the morning's fight.
Col. Delacroix had no new orders and held his line, content to let the cavalry do the chasing.

Maj. Verneuil was off the moment the order came. He rode into the fleeing battalion on the road, cut down the stragglers and rounded up about sixty prisoners. Nearing the line of the northern wood, he saw a fresh battalion formed in line across the road ahead. A volley emptied a few saddles. As ordered, he would not charge formed infantry, so he wheeled about and brought his prisoners back to the bridge.
units.departure: The engine had the squadron ride up to a formed line and trade carbine fire with it for ten minutes until it broke. The order says to come back on meeting formed infantry, so it turned back after one volley, losing 9 men, and ends at the bridge, active and in good heart.

units.account: Col. Brandt could not rally his men under the sabres of the pursuing horse. About sixty were taken and some twenty cut down before the fugitives streamed through the gaps in the Line Battalion. Behind its cover he is gathering what is left near the rally point, but the men are not yet steady.
units.departure: The engine rallied the battalion at minute 6, while enemy cavalry were among its fugitives. Being ridden down and losing about 80 men, 60 of them taken prisoner, it stays broken this turn, though the pursuit has stopped and it is near its rally point. The prisoners also make the loss larger than the engine's.

units.account: Col. Hartmann did it by the book. He shifted his line west to straddle the road, opened files for the Vanguard's fugitives to pass, and closed them again. When the enemy horse came on he gave them a volley at about 130 m, and they turned back. He holds the road.
Maj. von Reiter had no orders and held his squadron west of the road, watching the Vanguard stream back.
units.departure: The engine sent the squadron, which had no orders, over the bridge and through the Blue line to (2050,1766). It had no orders and could not have passed the bridge through the enemy, so it stayed put.

summary: Turn 2 (20-40). Blue's cavalry squadron received its pursuit order at minute 2 and rode into Red's broken Vanguard on the high road. It cut down about 20 and took about 60 prisoners. Red's Line Battalion received its order at minute 3, shifted west to straddle the road at (2050,750) and let the fugitives pass through. Nearing the line of the northern wood around minute 7, the squadron met this formed line, took a volley at about 130 m and lost 9 men. As its order required, it came back on meeting formed infantry, bringing its prisoners to the north end of the bridge. The Vanguard, down to about 300 men, is still broken but out of reach, gathering near its rally point at about (2000,450). Blue's two battalions held south of the bridge. Red's hussars stayed west of the road without orders. The engine's projection was rejected: it had the squadron stand ten minutes in a firefight until it broke, and the hussars ride through the Blue position.
